chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not leave his pubic hair for more than forty days, and it is not permissible for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to leave that from her for more than twenty days.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the maximum time one should leave pubic hair unremoved?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi links personal hygiene (fitrah) directly to theological conviction, establishing a specific temporal limit for grooming as a marker of piety. While the text specifies forty days for men and twenty for women, Shia scholars often contextualize this within the broader concept of 'fitrah' (natural disposition), emphasizing that neglecting such grooming is a sign of spiritual neglect. The distinction in duration may reflect practical considerations or differing scholarly interpretations regarding the urgency of the act for each gender.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrhim, form his father, from Al Nowfaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who was a believer in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Last Day, so he should not leave his pubic hair for more than forty days, nor is it Permissible for a woman who believes in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Last Day that she should leave that from her for more than twenty days’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘

One who believes in Allah and in the Day of Judgment, must not keep his pubic hairs for more than forty days. It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and in the Day of Judgment to keep that in her case for more than twenty days.’”
